slides.headline: 6 BUSINESS DOCUMENTS AI WRITES SO GOOD THEY FEEL ILLEGAL
slides.image_prompt: Thick stack of business documents marked with icons (dollar, warning triangle, X), electric-orange and slate-blue neon interior, desktop composition, zero readable text

slides.headline: 1) GENERATE A CLIENT PROPOSAL IN 10 MINUTES
slides.body: Consultants charge $200 to $400 to write one client proposal. This prompt writes the same document in 10 minutes: "I'm pitching [service] to [client]. Write a one-page proposal with a clear next step."

slides.headline: 2) BUILD A JOB POST THAT FILTERS BAD HIRES OUT
slides.body: A bad hire costs 30% of that person's first-year salary, per SHRM. This prompt writes a job post that filters candidates out before the first interview: "Write a job post for a [role] at [company type]. List 3 must-haves, 2 deal-breakers that screen people out, and one clear application step."

slides.headline: 3) TURN ANY MEETING INTO A DECISIONS-ONLY DOCUMENT
slides.body: The average manager wastes 31 hours a month in meetings where nothing gets recorded. This prompt strips any notes down to decisions made, owners, and deadlines: "Here are my meeting notes: [paste notes]. Pull out only: decisions made, who owns each one, and the deadline. Bullet list only."

slides.headline: 4) WRITE THE POLICY YOUR BUSINESS RUNS ON
slides.body: Most owners pay a consultant $300 to $600 to draft a single policy they never update. This prompt writes one that protects you in a dispute and reads as fair to clients: "Write a [policy type] policy for a [business type]. Protect the business in disputes, read as fair to clients, keep it under one page."

slides.headline: 5) WRITE AN SOP FOR ANY PROCESS YOU DO TWICE
slides.body: Writing one SOP manually takes a manager 3 to 4 hours. This prompt builds one for any task you describe, steps, one decision point per step, written for a new hire: "Write an SOP for [process]. Number every step. Include one decision point per step. Write it for someone on day one."

slides.headline: 6) WRITE A PERFORMANCE REVIEW THAT ACTUALLY LANDS
slides.body: Managers spend an average of 3 hours per review writing something the employee reads once and forgets. This prompt writes one that sticks in under 2 minutes: "Write a performance review for [name], a [role]. Top achievement: [achievement]. Growth area: [area]. Make it specific enough they still remember it next quarter."

slides.body:
